_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

`plan.md` is a **backend-only** plan. Frontend is out of scope. RAG (D–F) is written but **blocked** until Phase C is marked complete **and** you confirm in chat.

There are **six lettered phases**, with B split into five slices:

| Phase | What it is | Status in the plan |
|--------|------------|--------------------|
| **A** | Application setup: Maven Wrapper, Boot config, Compose Postgres, Liquibase ticket tables, Testcontainers smoke. Empty HTTP surface; no ticket APIs yet. | not started |
| **B** | Ticket **CRUD** (no status transitions). | — |
| **B1** | Domain enums, constants, sort whitelist. | not started |
| **B2** | Persistence entities and repositories. | not started |
| **B3** | DTOs, mapping, validation, CRUD application service. | not started |
| **B4** | Controllers, query validation, error handling. | not started |
| **B5** | Persistence across restart. | not started |
| **C** | State machine and legal PATCH `status` (T1–T5; illegal pairs → 409). | not started; **RAG gate** |
| **D** | RAG ingestion, embeddings, PgVector schema. | blocked |
| **E** | Ingest wiring from ticket service (after-commit hooks). | blocked |
| **F** | AI ask API (`POST /api/ai/ask`, retrieve-then-generate). | blocked |

**Order:** A → B1–B5 → C → **stop for your confirmation** → D → E → F.

Phase C is the hard gate (**G7** + **G8**): no Spring AI, embeddings, vector table use, or `/api/ai/ask` until C is complete and you say to start RAG.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Spring Boot 3.5.16 is the latest general availability release.

Generating the Maven project via start.spring.io with Spring Boot 3.5.16.

The generated project includes web, JPA, validation, Liquibase, PostgreSQL, and Testcontainers dependencies. A manual pom.xml with Maven wrapper is a fallback if Spring Boot 3.5.16 is unavailable. Testcontainers integration for Spring Boot 3.5 is being configured.

Testcontainers dependencies are scoped to test. The PostgreSQL container uses the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image. Liquibase will run before Hibernate validate. With no entities in Phase A, Hibernate validate will pass without errors.

Jackson will serialize dates as ISO-8601 UTC strings rather than timestamps. Hibernate ddl-auto is set to validate. The database timezone is UTC. Unknown properties will cause deserialization failures. Default property inclusion is left as-is.

A ConfigurationProperties record will hold API pagination defaults. The default page size is 20 and the maximum is 100. Relaxed YAML binding maps these values automatically. The PostgreSQL datasource URL will use a localhost fallback with environment variable support.

Local database credentials will default to "tickets" in both the YAML and Docker Compose files. Environment variables will override these defaults at runtime. The .env.example file will document the required variable names. Local defaults match the Compose configuration so the application starts immediately after docker compose up.

Docker Compose mounts a named volume for PostgreSQL data persistence. Liquibase will define a descending index on the ticket table's created_at column. GIN indexes require raw SQL changesets.

Liquibase will run three changelogs in sequence: 001 for the ticket tables, 002 for extensions, and 003 for indexes. The master changelog includes each file in order. A GIN trigram index on the title column will use pg_trgm. The pg_trgm extension will be created if missing. The ticket number sequence starts at 1001.

PostgreSQL UUID type is used for ticket identifiers. Liquibase is enabled by pointing to the master changelog on the classpath. A smoke test will use Testcontainers to spin up a PostgreSQL container and dynamically inject its JDBC URL into Spring Boot properties.

The Testcontainers smoke test will also inject the container's username and password dynamically. It will verify schema application by querying information_schema.tables for the ticket table and checking the ticket_number_seq sequence value. Spring-JDBC is already included through the data-jpa dependency.

The smoke test will also verify indexes on the ticket and ticket_comment tables. Backend target directories are already excluded by the global .gitignore. The .env file will be omitted from version control. A brief backend README will be added for local startup instructions. Graphify will be updated after code changes. The Maven wrapper will be generated from the Spring Initializer zip. Default Application.java from the generator will be excluded if the package name is incorrect. The repository root will be checked for a parent POM.
</details></think>

Status and priority columns will be NOT NULL without database defaults; the application will supply OPEN and MEDIUM values. Liquibase changelog comments will follow the spec SQL format. GIN index creation will use a PostgreSQL-specific SQL changeset. ChangeSet 002 must execute before 003 because the GIN index depends on pg_trgm.

Liquibase YAML includes will use `relativeToChangelogFile: true`. The Maven wrapper properties will reference Maven 3.9.11 and wrapper 3.3.2. Proceeding to write all files now.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reading the API contract sort whitelist.

Planning the B1 implementation. SortParser will reside in the api package since sorting is an HTTP concern. Domain classes will include TicketStatus, TicketPriority, TicketCategory, and TicketId. The whitelist covers createdAt, updatedAt, priority, and status. A constants class will define the TicketId format and maximum lengths. Unit tests for SortParser are also planned.

TicketPriority will carry a sortRank() method for ascending priority ordering. TicketId will expose a static format() helper that rejects values below 1001 and prefixes numbers with TKT-. Parsing support is omitted to keep B1 lean.

A custom JSON deserializer for TicketPriority is being drafted. It normalizes legacy "URGENT" and "CRITICAL" strings to the CRITICAL enum constant, then delegates to standard valueOf parsing for remaining inputs.

The deserializer will throw a JsonMappingException for unknown priorities. Jackson’s default enum serializer already emits uppercase values, so no custom serializer is needed. The component will register via JacksonConfig, and DTOs will apply @JsonDeserialize annotations.

The deserializer will be a global `@JsonComponent` bean in the api package, ensuring JPA does not bypass Jackson. A `TicketConstraints` constants class will define field limits: title 500 characters, description 100,000, and assignee 320.

TicketConstraints now includes comment body and resolution notes limits. SortParser will split the sort string on the first comma, validate the property against the whitelist, and default to descending direction.

Spring Data Sort will stay out of the domain layer. SortParser and SortWhitelist will be placed in a small api.common package under the api ticket module. Invalid sort exceptions will use a simple IllegalArgumentException for B1 unit testing, with HTTP mapping deferred to B4.

SortWhitelist will be a named domain type rather than a small api common package. SortParser will also live in the domain package without Spring dependencies. It will return a lightweight record containing the property and direction, with a local enum for direction values.

The default sort is createdAt,desc. Invalid sorts will throw IllegalArgumentException with a message for later HTTP mapping. Checking the API contract to confirm the default direction when only a property is provided.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Phase B1 is done.** Domain closed sets, id/sort helpers, and `URGENT` JSON mapping are in place. No entities, services, HTTP, or state machine yet.

**Domain** (`com.ticketmanagement.domain`)
- `TicketStatus`: `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`, `CANCELLED`
- `TicketPriority`: `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL` only (no `URGENT`); sort order 1–4
- `TicketCategory`: `PAYMENTS`, `SHIPMENT`, `BILLING`, `LOGIN`, `OTHER`
- `TicketId.format` → `TKT-{n}`; field max lengths; `SortParser` whitelist `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `priority`, `status` (default `createdAt,desc`)

The `TicketEntity` maps its `comments` collection with `@OneToMany` and `orphanRemoval`. `CommentEntity` will use `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.UUID)` for its primary key. It will reference `TicketEntity` via `@ManyToOne` with a required foreign key. Java beans will provide getters and setters instead of Lombok. `equals` and `hashCode` will rely on the generated ID after persistence.

Standard getters and setters will be used instead of public fields. A convenience `addComment` method will be added to `TicketEntity` to manage bidirectional relationships. The error envelope structure comes from api-standards. The PATCH empty body requirement comes from api-contract 4.

Jackson deserializes an empty PATCH body to all-null fields. Null values will be treated as omitted during merge. A dedicated EmptyPatchException will be created to reject empty PATCH requests.

Domain exceptions TicketNotFoundException and IllegalTicketTransitionException are defined. Error envelope records include ErrorBody, ErrorResponse, DataResponse, PageResponse, and PageMeta. The api-standards error details shape still needs definition.

Pagination defaults are page 0 and size 20, capped at 100. TicketListQuery enforces these bounds via annotations. Invalid status parameters trigger 400 validation errors. Jackson will reject unknown properties on DTOs.

Spring Boot 3 does not fail on unknown properties by default. The ObjectMapper must be explicitly configured to throw errors for unknown properties on DTOs.

Jackson unknown-property rejection will be applied globally in JacksonConfig for version one tickets. The TicketPriority deserializer is already registered globally. UpdateTicketRequest title validation uses @Size(max=500) to permit null while allowing empty strings. A @NotBlank constraint will be added to reject empty titles.

Assignee fields will be limited to 320 characters on both create and update operations. The TicketService implementation begins with transactional creation logic that formats ticket IDs, trims titles, and normalizes null descriptions to empty strings.

Created tickets default to OPEN status and MEDIUM priority when omitted. The getById method will fetch comments separately and sort them. The list endpoint clamps page and size defaults, parses sort parameters, and applies search filtering. The updateFields method throws EmptyPatchException for empty PATCH bodies, loads the existing ticket, merges only non-null fields, and persists the entity.

addComment loads the ticket, appends the comment, and cascades the save. The ticket entity updates its timestamp via @PreUpdate. New comments return 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the comment resource. The controller builds that URL using ServletUriComponentsBuilder. RestExceptionHandler must extract the request path from HttpServletRequest or ServletWebRequest. Error timestamps are UTC Instants. Slice tests use @WebMvcTest on the controller and import JacksonConfig, WebCorsConfig, and RestExceptionHandler. They mock TicketService.

Controller-level pagination constraints will use `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "0")` and `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "20")` with `@Min(0)` and `@Max(100)`. The controller class needs `@Validated` so Spring validates these parameters. A `size` of zero triggers a 400 `ConstraintViolationException`.

Integration tests will extend `AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest` and use `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` with `@Testcontainers`. Extra fields in requests will return 400. The plan requires running `review-code` on the diff and fixing failures before Phase C.

TicketMapper will be a @Component in the service package. Its toDetail method converts entities to responses, sorts comments by creation date, and maps each comment individually.

The getById endpoint will lazily load comments via findWithCommentsById. The list endpoint will map summaries without joining comments. To guarantee blank titles never persist, the service layer itself will validate titles rather than relying solely on controller Bean Validation. Service unit tests using Mockito will verify that blank titles are rejected and that valid titles proceed to save.

The service layer will guard against blank titles by throwing an exception when the title is null or empty. This keeps the API as the primary validation boundary while adding a safety net in the service. Service unit tests will verify that blank titles prevent the repository save call.

A custom `TicketValidationException` will carry field details for validation failures. The REST exception handler will map this exception to a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` response.

Malformed JSON, size zero, and size one hundred and one will be tested. @WebMvcTest will import JacksonConfig and RestExceptionHandler explicitly.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Planning to implement a restart test.

Spring caches ApplicationContext by default, so a second @SpringBootTest would reuse the same context instead of restarting. Adding @DirtiesContext to the first test class will force a fresh context and verify the ticket persists across restarts.

The implementation uses a nested `@SpringBootTest` inside `TicketRestartIT`. The first nested class creates the ticket and stores its ID in a static field. A second nested class then verifies the ticket persists across restarts. `@DirtiesContext` is applied to the first test method to force a fresh context.

Nested classes complicate sharing the Testcontainers `@Container` and applying `@DynamicPropertySource` correctly. A simpler alternative is to use a flat `@SpringBootTest` with `@DirtiesContext(classMode = AFTER_CLASS)` instead of nested classes.

A flat two-class design is preferable. One class writes the ticket and stores its ID. Another reads it back. Both extend the same abstract test class. Spring may run the read class before the write class alphabetically. This ordering could cause issues.

ReadIT runs before WriteIT alphabetically. Renaming to TicketRestart1WriteIT and TicketRestart2ReadIT fixes the ordering problem. The preferred design is a single flat class with a static persistedId field. The first test stores the ticket ID and applies @DirtiesContext(methodMode = AFTER_METHOD) to force a fresh context.

`@DirtiesContext(methodMode = AFTER_METHOD)` closes the Spring context after the first test and starts a fresh one for the second test in the same class. This matches the plan's nested class approach but avoids nested class complexity. `@TestMethodOrder(OrderAnnotation.class)` is required to enforce execution order.

The static PostgreSQL container survives context recreation. Liquibase skips reapplication because the changelog table already exists. Hibernate validation passes cleanly. The test will use MockMvc to perform a GET request. Implementation goes into `TicketRestartIT.java`. Plan.md B5 checkboxes and Phase B status will be updated. Phase C is deferred. Graphification follows.

Adding `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` directly to `TicketRestartIT`, since `AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest` does not include it. The class declares static fields for the persisted ticket ID and comment body, autowires `MockMvc`, and begins the first test with `@Order(1)` and `@DirtiesContext(methodMode = AFTER_METHOD)`.

The first test posts a ticket with a unique "restart-persist-ticket" title and a comment, extracting the ID via JSON path. The second test fetches the ticket by ID and asserts the title and comment body. A JSON helper from TicketApiIT will be reused.

The test will be implemented and executed now. The plan sign-off table will be updated. A concern arose that `@DirtiesContext` on this class might dirty the shared Spring context cache used by other integration tests, though the default cache key is the test class itself.

Spring Boot Test context cache keys include the test class itself. Because TicketApiIT and TicketRestartIT are separate classes, they typically hold independent ApplicationContext instances. DirtiesContext on the restart test will therefore not dirty the API integration test's context.

The shared static PostgreSQL container means data written by the restart test persists for later API integration tests. The GET request targets a unique ticket ID, so cross-test contamination is avoided. I will implement the file now, using JsonPath helpers from TicketApiIT. Both B5 and CRUD FEAT-01-10 will be marked complete in the plan status line.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing the state-machine documentation sections 5.6 and 6.

Planning the TicketStatusMachine implementation. Five statuses yield 25 pairs total, 5 legal and 20 illegal. Drafting a static `assertTransitionAllowed` method. Considering null handling for current and target statuses. Reviewing PATCH presence, §8 placement, and test helpers.

Null handling for the transition machine is unnecessary because PATCH deserialization distinguishes a missing field from an invalid one. The machine throws `IllegalTicketTransitionException` for illegal pairs including self-transitions. The service layer will check for updates first, then locate the ticket, and finally invoke the machine. Empty patches return 400 before the find step; status-only patches proceed to lookup.

The transition check runs before other field updates. If the status change is illegal, the remaining fields are skipped and the ticket is not saved. Field-only PATCHes bypass the machine entirely. To support service tests that verify the machine is not called, the class should be an instance rather than a static utility.

Decided against static methods for the transition machine to keep the domain free of Spring. TicketService will instead receive a package-private instance via constructor injection. This allows tests to verify the machine is used without requiring Spring configuration.

Reconsidering the static approach. A static machine avoids Spring bean configuration entirely. Tests can simply assert the status remains unchanged during a field-only PATCH. This removes the need for constructor injection or instance creation.

Settled on a final `TicketStatusMachine` instance with an extra constructor for tests. Checking whether `TicketEntity` uses a JPA `@PreUpdate` hook to manage `updatedAt`.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Spring failed to instantiate TicketService due to two constructors. It may be attempting to use a default constructor.

Spring Boot 3 greedily selected the four-argument package-private constructor. It falls back to no-arg instantiation because TicketStatusMachine is not a bean. This triggers the "No default constructor found" error.

Spring likely skipped constructor autowiring because both constructors were ambiguous. Adding `@Autowired` to the three-argument public constructor would resolve the ambiguity. Alternatively, keeping only one public constructor—such as the three-argument version—would prevent Spring from choosing the four-argument package-private method.

The best approach is a single three-argument constructor with a package-private field for test injection. This avoids Spring autowiring ambiguity entirely. The status machine should remain a plain object with no Spring dependencies.
</details></think>

Planning the test generation workflow.

Only gaps remain to be written. CRUD and state machine scenarios are already fully covered. Ask and RAG ingest are not yet implemented.

Two gaps stand out. A single integration test should cover the full lifecycle flow from OPEN through T1–T3 to X1. Service-layer legal transitions are currently only tested for T1; all five edges must be validated across every application layer.

Commenting on CLOSED or CANCELLED is a positive edge case missing from tests. PATCH on CLOSED is another allowed but untested scenario. The IN_PROGRESS list filter after T1 is an edge combination to cover. Service-layer legal transitions T2 through T5 will be parameterized with a small MethodSource.

Slice-level T1 200 mapping is optional P1. updatedAt advancement on legal transitions is optional. Create must not invoke the state machine; a service spy will verify this. The planned files are TicketApiIT for lifecycle Flow A and parameterized CLOSED and CANCELLED comment and PATCH tests, plus TicketServiceTest for parameterized T2–T5 legal transitions and the no-machine-call assertion.

TicketControllerSliceTest will verify the legal T1 200 envelope. Ask and RAG ingest are excluded. Existing API helpers will be reused. Tests will stay minimal. The lifecycle test asserts a 409 when reopening a closed ticket. A parameterized test will cover commenting and PATCHing on CLOSED and CANCELLED.

The parameterized test will reuse `ticketIn` to create a ticket at the target terminal status, then patch its title and post a comment, asserting the response includes both updates while the status remains unchanged. For service-layer legal transitions beyond T1, the test will set the entity status to the source state before patching to the destination, then verify the save persists. The create-no-machine-call assertion will use a spy to ensure `assertTransitionAllowed` is never invoked during creation.

The slice test needs a way to build a TicketDetailResponse with a non-OPEN status. The existing `detail()` helper hardcodes OPEN, so an overload or new helper is required to support IN_PROGRESS.

Adding spring-ai-starter-model-ollama and the Spring AI BOM to satisfy plan 10.4. Tests will default to localhost:11434 with nomic-embed-text.

The auto-configured EmbeddingModel could fail at startup if Ollama is unreachable. To keep smoke tests offline, the starter will be excluded and the adapter bean will be conditional on the EmbeddingModel class. Test profiles may also disable OllamaAutoConfiguration via properties.

Defaulting `spring.ai.model.embedding` to `none` in application.yml would break production Docker setups. A dedicated `rag.embedding` configuration block is preferred instead.

The `rag.embedding.enabled` flag will gate the Ollama adapter bean. When disabled, a stub port throws an exception on embed, which is safe because smoke tests never call ingest. The implementation will use RestClient for direct `/api/embeddings` POST rather than Spring AI initially, though the plan expects Spring AI.

The Spring AI BOM will be locked to version 1.0.2. Maven compatibility will be verified before proceeding.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
TicketIngestionIT persist generates ticket IDs using TKT-1000 plus count. This risks collisions with sequence tickets from other tests sharing the same Spring context database.

TicketApiIT also creates tickets, so TKT-1001 from sequence collides with TKT-1001 from count. A UUID-based fake ID would exceed the VARCHAR(16) limit. The chosen approach is TKT-8 plus ten digits from the last ten digits of System.nanoTime(), yielding exactly sixteen characters.

The cleaner fix for TicketIngestionIT is to use `tickets.nextTicketNumber()` and `TicketId.format()` instead of generating fake IDs manually. TicketChunkerTest needs its overflow comment shortened from 26 characters to 20. A regex for comment lines in the Comments section also needs updating. An unused `RagProperties` import in `KnowledgeDocumentBuilderTest` should be removed.

JdbcVectorChunkStore contains an unused ArrayList that should be checked. The integration test second ingest may still yield one chunk if min-chars merging applies. The assertion "greaterThanOrEqualTo firstCount" remains valid because IDs differ. Empty string persists require the description embeddable to be false.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing TicketServiceTest, RestExceptionHandler, CreateTicketRequest, TicketIngestionIT, HashEmbeddingPort, AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest, TicketControllerSliceTest, and architecture 15.

Evaluating how to handle ingest hooks in unit tests where `TransactionSynchronizationManager.afterCommit` may not fire without Spring transactions. Considering either conditional registration based on active synchronization, immediate ingestion in tests, or using `TransactionTemplate` in integration tests. The specification requires `afterCommit` so ingest failures do not roll back the ticket transaction.

Settled on a conditional approach. The `ingestAfterCommit` method checks `TransactionSynchronizationManager.isSynchronizationActive()` before registering the `afterCommit` callback. When synchronization is inactive, ingestion runs immediately. This satisfies both the transaction rollback requirement and unit test isolation.

The `ingestSafely` helper wraps ingestion in a try-catch block to prevent ingest failures from rolling back the ticket transaction. Validation errors, illegal transitions, and blank titles all occur before the ticket is saved, so ingest is never scheduled. Failed embedding is caught safely after the ticket commits. Integration tests rely on Spring's `@Transactional` to ensure `afterCommit` fires only after the transaction completes.

Realized that `@Transactional` on `@SpringBootTest` methods can roll back the transaction, preventing `afterCommit` from firing. `TicketIngestionIT` currently calls `ingest()` directly, but `TicketApiIT` with ingest hooks would fail under the same conditions. Need to inspect `AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest` to see how it handles transactions.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
UnrecognizedPropertyException handling is needed. FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES is already enabled.

RestExceptionHandler needs updating to map UnrecognizedPropertyException to VALIDATION_ERROR instead of BAD_REQUEST. Existing tests may expect BAD_REQUEST for unknown properties. TicketId will be logged via MDC correlation id. Cosine similarity search will use PostgreSQL vector operators in JDBC.

RetrievedChunk will hold ticketId, content, and similarity. PostgreSQL cosine distance returns 1 minus cosine similarity. HashEmbeddingPort uses sparse one-hot vectors, so identical text hashes to the same slot with similarity 1, while different text typically yields 0. This means a query like "payment gateway" may fail to match a ticket containing "payment gateway timeout" if their hash slots differ.

Band A will use stubbed retrieval and generation ports. Unit tests will mock VectorChunkStore.search and GenerationPort. An integration test can verify semantic similarity by posting a question identical to the ticket description, provided GenerationPort is stubbed with @Primary. Without that stub, GenerationPort throws.

TicketService needs a new required collaborator, TicketIngestionService. The constructor will expand from four arguments to five. TicketIngestionService will trigger vector ingestion after ticket commits. AskService, the AI ask controller, request/response data objects, and generation port stubs are next. Tests will cover the full flow.

The UnrecognizedPropertyException handler will be inserted before InvalidFormatException in RestExceptionHandler. TicketServiceTest must pass a mock TicketIngestionService. RestExceptionHandlerTest will gain coverage for unknown properties through AskController. MDC correlation logging will be skipped unless a correlation ID is already present. The chat prompt will remain internal and not be exposed in the API.

The chat prompt will instruct the LLM to answer using only retrieved ticket excerpts and cite only the provided ticket IDs. AskService will ignore any citations generated by the LLM and rely solely on retrieved chunks. If generation throws, the service returns a 500 error. When no chunks match, generation is skipped entirely. For requirement G-03, cited ticket IDs must exist in the database, so the system will either filter retrieved chunks against existing tickets or ensure the vector store only contains valid ticket IDs.

GenerationPort.generate will accept a question and a list of RetrievedChunk objects. Vector search returns a ranked list, so retrieved chunks will be deduplicated in relevance order. Stale citations from deleted tickets are acceptable because no delete API exists. Existing ticket tests that submit unknown JSON properties may need updates, since those currently return 400 BAD_REQUEST but should now return VALIDATION_ERROR under the new exception handler.
</details></think>

Considering whether to add `rag.generation.no-match-answer` as a configuration option.

The no-match phrase will be a constant in AskService to match the specification exactly. Chat model configuration will be added to YAML later. C-04 remains open, so the disabled generation port stays. Search needs to be implemented on JdbcVectorChunkStore. Spring Boot auto-configures JdbcTemplate with Data JPA.

Cosine similarity equals 1 minus pgvector cosine distance. The filter threshold is 0.72. Hash matches score 1.0. Non-matches score 0.0. Ask IT uses exact text as description. TicketIngestionIT and TicketApiIT will trigger ingestion on ticket creation. The disabled embedding port would throw errors on embeddable tickets.

AfterCommit hooks run before the HTTP response is sent. If ingestion throws an uncaught exception there, the request will 500. Otherwise the HTTP 201 response is already committed.

Checking Spring's TransactionSynchronizationUtils to confirm whether afterCommit exceptions propagate to the caller. This determines if ingestion errors must be caught explicitly within the hook.

Spring logs and swallows afterCommit exceptions, so ingestion failures won't 500 the request. Still, wrapping the hook in try/catch is needed to emit a proper ERROR log with the ticket ID.

To avoid noisy ERROR logs during tests, HashEmbeddingPort should be set as the primary embedding port in test configuration. This would let all integration tests use hash embeddings instead of the disabled port.

A shared test configuration will import both HashEmbeddingPort and StubGenerationPort. The latter returns a stubbed answer. AskServiceTest will mock the store, embedding, and generation ports.

TicketService afterCommit unit tests will run without a transaction, so ingestion happens immediately. A mock ingestion port will throw to simulate failure. The create method still returns successfully because ingestSafely catches the error. Failed writes will skip ingestion entirely. A Mock TicketIngestionService is required in TicketServiceTest.

The TicketService constructor will gain a fifth parameter for ingestion. All existing constructors must be updated accordingly.

TicketIngestionHookIT will extend AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest and use HashEmbeddingPort. It will verify that updating a ticket description writes the new content to the vector store.

Closing a ticket will set its metadata to CLOSED.

Hardening failed embedding scenarios in integration tests is difficult. Unit tests on the service layer are sufficient.

Unit tests will cover Jdbc search and cosine parsing. AskIT will provide the integration test.

Jackson 2 will throw UnrecognizedPropertyException for unknown fields. AskRequest is a record with a validated question field. The AiAskController exposes POST /api/ai/ask and /api/v1/ai/ask. It trims the question before passing it to the service. AskResponseData holds the answer and cited ticket IDs.

Existing tickets are ingested, so retrieved citation IDs are assumed to exist. The service will not perform extra existence checks on those IDs. If no chunks remain after retrieval, it will fall back to the no-match answer.

AskService embeds the question, searches the vector store, deduplicates cited ticket IDs, and generates an answer. An empty generation result still returns a grounded response with citations. The generation port receives structured context to prevent prompt injection. JdbcVectorChunkStore.searchSimilar will accept a float array query, topK, and minimum similarity threshold.

The SQL query casts the query vector to pgvector and orders by cosine distance. Two placeholders are needed for the cast expression.

The vector search query will cast the same query vector twice. The topK limit comes from YAML and defaults to 8. Ingestion is skipped for get and list operations. Create and updateField operations schedule ingestion after saving. Comment addition triggers ingestion after flush. Ingestion failures will log the ticket ID via MDC. A placeholder for the chat model will be added to YAML without selecting a live provider, since C-04 is still open.

Spring AI is still not integrated. The TicketService constructor change could break other callers, so all existing usages must be located first. The test configuration will be placed in the support package and imported by AbstractPostgresIntegrationTest. Plan.md will be updated at the end of the phase.

AskServiceTest will be a plain unit test without Spring. AskControllerSliceTest will use WebMvcTest. AskApiIT will cover both POST routes. JdbcVectorChunkStoreTest may be added directly to AskApiIT. TicketServiceTest will verify ingestion is skipped for empty titles, unknown comments, missing tickets, and invalid transitions. TicketIngestionHookIT will verify updates write new content to the vector store.

A `fieldOnlyPatch` update will trigger ingestion. The `retrievedChunk` type will be a record on `VectorChunkStore`. `EmbeddingPort` will expose a single-question `embed` method alongside `embedAll`, throwing if the result is empty. `DisabledGenerationPort` will reside in the `rag` package. `AskService` will be implemented next. The `lean-build` file will be skipped per the user's explicit instruction.

Unknown properties will return VALIDATION_ERROR instead of BAD_REQUEST. Ask integration tests will assert this error. The .env.example will leave OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL empty. Unused generation properties will be skipped until a live adapter is added. Only TicketServiceTest needs constructor updates.

The three-argument constructor will delegate to a new four-argument constructor that injects `TicketIngestionService`. This avoids breaking existing production callers. There is no circular dependency because the ingestion service only depends on `TicketRepository`, not on `TicketService` itself. The `TransactionSynchronization` import is needed for the after-commit hook. Default `REQUIRED` propagation is sufficient even with nested transactions. Jdbc cosine search tests will be written inside `AskApiIT`.

AskRequest will enforce a 2000-character limit and reject blank questions. Unknown properties will fail validation, while malformed JSON returns 400. Both API routes will be parameterized. AskServiceTest will verify that generation is never invoked when no chunks are retrieved. The stubbed generation port will receive only the retrieved excerpts. AskApiIT will be read-only, counting tickets before and after the call to ensure no mutations occur.

RestExceptionHandler will map Jackson UnrecognizedPropertyException to a validation error response. The test configuration will use a non-primary HashEmbeddingPort bean, but ApplicationSmokeTest and TicketApiIT will rely on it being primary so the ingestion hook can resolve it. TicketApiIT will ingest newly created tickets, which adds a small overhead. All remaining files will be implemented in a single batch.

Phase E and F will be marked complete in plan.md once tests pass. AskService will inject RagProperties to retrieve the topK limit. The graphify update will be applied at the end of the phase.

The vector store will always use cosine distance regardless of any configured metric. TicketServiceTest will mock TicketIngestionService and verify ingestion is triggered after create and updateField. It will also verify ingestion is skipped for emptyPatch, illegalTransition, blankTitle, unknown ticket, and list operations. The test will cover ingestion failure handling.

TicketServiceTest will simulate ingestion failures by throwing a RuntimeException inside the mocked ingest call, then assert that the ticket is still created successfully. TicketIngestionHookIT will verify that updating a ticket description replaces the existing vector chunks.

TicketIngestionHookIT will verify that a rewritten description is stored as a new vector chunk. A close-refresh test will confirm that status metadata updates correctly through IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, and CLOSED transitions. AskApiIT will test a targeted exact-phrase lookup against a fresh ticket, plus a fallback for queries against an empty corpus.

AskApiIT will verify that no-match and below-threshold queries never invoke generation. The stubbed answer will be asserted as a plain string rather than a golden LLM paragraph. Both API routes will be tested. AskServiceTest will verify citation order. The retrieved chunk type will be defined.

Citation order will be [T2, T1] when T2 scores 0.9, T1 scores 0.85, and T2 scores 0.8. RestExceptionHandler will map UnrecognizedPropertyException to VALIDATION_ERROR with the offending property name. Ready to write the files.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

**Phases E and F are in place.** `./mvnw test` is green. Changes are **not committed**.

**Phase E — ingest after ticket writes**
- `TicketService` schedules ingest on create, PATCH (including status-only / close), and comments, **after commit**.
- Embed/store failures are logged and **do not roll back** the ticket.
- Failed writes (validation, illegal transition, missing ticket) **never** call ingest.

**Phase F — ask API**
- `POST /api/ai/ask` and `POST /api/v1/ai/ask` share one handler.
- Body is only `question` (blank / missing / >2000 / unknown properties → **400**).
- Grounded **200**: `data.answer` + `data.citedTicketIds` from retrieval order, deduped.
- No hits (or below `rag.retrieval.similarity-threshold`) → **200** `"No relevant tickets found."` and **no** generate call.
- Ask does not create or update tickets.

**Still not live models:** production still uses disabled embed/generate ports. Tests use hash embeddings and a stub generator. Spring AI / Ollama chat (**C-04**) is not wired.

Say if you want a commit, `/review-code`, or a live Ollama adapter next.

Tests will continue to rely on the `Hash` double as the primary implementation.

The plan now restores `DisabledEmbeddingPort` with `@ConditionalOnMissingBean(EmbeddingPort.class)`. The Ollama embedding adapter will use `@ConditionalOnBean(EmbeddingModel.class)`. In production, the Ollama bean is created first. The disabled bean is then skipped because the interface already exists. Tests will keep the `Hash` double as primary and disable Spring AI models to prevent the Ollama adapter from being created.

The `DisabledEmbeddingPort` will be skipped entirely when `HashEmbeddingPort` is present. `ConditionalOnMissingBean` checks the `EmbeddingPort` type, and since `Hash` already implements that interface, the disabled bean is never created. This avoids duplicate beans and injection conflicts in tests.

Slice tests will not load the full Spring context. ApplicationSmokeTest extends AbstractPostgres and relies on the Hash double without live Ollama. Production will activate the Ollama embedding port once the Spring AI EmbeddingModel is present. To avoid startup failures when Ollama is unavailable, the pull-model strategy will be set to never.

The Ollama base URL will default to `http://localhost:11434` in the Spring properties. The chat model will remain environment-only with no default, requiring the user to set `OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL` themselves. A documented example will be added to `.env.example`.

The `.env.example` will use `${OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL:llama3.2}` as a convention default. This mirrors the architecture guidance without mandating a specific model. The chat model will remain environment-only.

RagProperties will keep its own embedding baseUrl and model fields. Spring AI properties will handle the actual Ollama model wiring. The application.yml will align rag.embedding.model with spring.ai.ollama.embedding.options.model. RagProperties will map baseUrl to spring.ai.ollama.base-url.

No Docker Compose file will be added for Ollama. The README will document the OLLAMA environment variables. An `application-test.yml` will disable Spring AI models by setting `spring.ai.model.chat` and `embedding` to `none`. Spring Boot automatically loads this file during tests, ensuring the Ollama adapters are never created in test contexts.

I will use `@TestPropertySource`, `DynamicPropertySource`, or `application-test.yml` with `@ActiveProfiles("test")` instead. I need to find all `@SpringBootTest` classes to apply the profile correctly.

Adding `@ActiveProfiles("test")` and `application-test.yml` alongside `DynamicPropertySource` on `AbstractPostgres` to disable chat and embedding models. `WebMvcTest` and `AiAskControllerSliceTest` will not load the full context or Ollama, so they remain unaffected.

Unit tests for adapters will use Mockito. `OllamaEmbeddingPort` will be simplified by removing the `toFloatArray` conversion if `getOutput()` already returns `float[]`.
